palette.notes: The article says mood can change by colour choice alone, but gives no ramp numbers.

lighting: Decide one light source before shading; overhead feels natural and the author usually puts the key light top-left or top-right for a dynamic but balanced read. Extra lights at lower intensity are allowed. Keep the concept simple and get contrast right.
silhouette: Not covered directly; light and cast shadows add the depth that keeps low-res shapes from looking flat.
texture: Shadow, mid-tone and highlight are suggested by managing colour clusters rather than gradients.

acting.enters: No characters described in the text.
acting.acts: Staging lesson: the light sets the mood (happy, relaxed, melancholy) through colour choice and cluster work.
acting.depth: Cast shadow quality tells the air: hazy = soft diffuse shadows, clear = hard crisp ones, space = long razor-sharp ones; cast shadows add depth where they help.

techniques: one key light fixed before any shading, top-left or top-right
secondary lights at lower intensity only
cast shadow softness matches the atmosphere (soft in haze, hard in clear air)
mood shift by palette change alone, same clusters
keep the light concept simple; contrast does the work
feel: one top-corner key light + cast shadows that match the air = depth and mood without detail
for_fred: Light Fred and Pixie from the same top corner as the reel's background and give each a cast/contact shadow on the ground or water; keep that light fixed across the reel so when Fred exits and comes back small in the background, the same light and a shorter, softer shadow sell the distance.
